name: Travel Food Services Ltd
title: Travel Food Services Ltd - 544443 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Travel F&B operator grew system-wide sales 18% and PAT 35.6% on flat traffic, but LFL slowed to 0.8% (7% ex-disrupted markets) and EBITDA margin fell to 35.8% on pre-opening costs for 87 new outlets.

triggers.label: Pre-opening costs lift employee and other costs
triggers.quote: EBITDA margin moderated to 35.8% for the quarter, reflecting the impact of higher employee cost and operating cost associated with recently commissioned airports

triggers.label: Price escalation held back this year
triggers.quote: we've not done a significant price escalation as well this year , with the challenge around it, we've been a bit tempered in that

triggers.label: H2 traffic bounce expected, unquantified

triggers.highlight: H2 of this year should be a good bounce back

guidance.quote: adjusted gross profit margin of around 81%, which remains well within our guided range

red_flags.quote: higher other income, which included a be nefit of INR131 million arising from write-back of a GST provision

summary.headline: Travel Food Services Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT up 35.6% YoY to INR1.3 billion on 20.6% revenue growth, despite flat passenger traffic and 0.8% system-wide LFL.
summary.overview: Management reported system-wide sales up 18% YoY to INR8.4 billion and consolidated revenue from operations up 20.6% YoY to INR4.5 billion, with net contract gains of 15.9% system-wide. Passenger traffic was broadly flat YoY, with international traffic hit by the Middle East conflict and May's domestic rebound reversed in June. EBITDA rose 11% to INR1.6 billion, but margin moderated to 35.8% on pre-operating and employee costs for new airports (Noida, Cochin, Delhi). PAT was helped by a INR131 million one-time GST provision write-back in other income.

financial_highlights.change: ex-Mumbai, Guwahati and some South India markets about 7%
Adjusted for INR223 million lounge aggregation cost reclassification: INR3.65 billion, about 81%
+35.6% YoY vs 25.3% margin last year; includes INR131 million GST provision write-back

segments.name: Travel QSR and lounges (system-wide)
segments.commentary: 580 outlets and lounges at June end across 21 airports; 153 brands; 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges added over last 12 months. Noida International Airport commenced operations in the quarter.

segments.name: JV / associate business
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 15% per management's implied figure as questioned by analysts; drag from Western India airports with Middle East exposure. Management said JV ramp-up continues.

segments.name: Passenger services (Elite Assist)
segments.commentary: Launched at Noida International Airport with meet-and-greet and porter services; to integrate into the EATS platform and expand to more airports.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 passenger traffic bounce-back as airlines restore long-haul international routes from September and October 2026.
About 90 units commissioned over last 12 months expected to normalise over next 12 months; benefits to play out in H2 FY27.
Over 50 outlets under development, mostly to open in FY27; 12-18 months to mature at existing terminals, 18-24 months at greenfield airports.
Pre-operating costs for Cochin, Delhi and Noida ramp-up expected to normalise in about 12 months, returning to traditional cost levels.
Delhi T3 contract runs to 30 September 2026; GHL JV bid result pending. Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28.
Bhogapuram Airport opened 17 August 2026 with multiple outlets under JV GHL.
capex_capacity: Over 50 outlets under construction or about to start construction across airports including Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Bhogapuram and Noida.
Noida International Airport outlets and passenger services commissioned in the quarter.
Asia focus for international expansion; Dubai entity set up for the Middle East and Indonesia entity set up recently to enable local bids.
Highways wayside amenities (WSA) under evaluation, with government plan of about 1,000 wayside amenities; management says medium-to-long term.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic broadly flat YoY in Q1: April declined, May rebounded to record domestic month, June softened on renewed conflict. Management says traffic in July-August similar to Q1 trend, with international the drag.
LFL growth normally runs 5-7 percentage points above passenger traffic; management did not take significant price increases this year, with growth from premiumisation, bundles and brand changes.
Mumbai and Guwahati hit by traffic migration to new airport infrastructure; South India markets hit by Middle East exposure.
Contract renewal rate moved from about 94% to 92%, attributed to non-renewal of small highway outlets.
Management says bidding discipline stays on cash return; net contract gains are lumpy and not guided.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 4.2% LFL came from higher spend per passenger, and what is sustainable LFL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LFL is typically 5-7 points above passenger traffic; it was 7% ex-affected markets. Growth came from premiumisation, bundles, brand edits and limited pricing, with price increases kept tempered.

qa_highlights.question: Lounge aggregation cost and other expenses rise in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost sits in other expenses; excluding it, other expenses rose 22% YoY. Management expects normalisation within about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are JV and associate revenues growing slower than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Some JV contracts are moving to JV structures over time, and Western airports with Middle East exposure, which form a bulk of JV portfolio, were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Delhi T3 contract moving to JV in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi T3 contract runs to 30 September 2026; GHL has bid and results are awaited. The new SPV with GMR has 30% TFS shareholding, so it will not be consolidated going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 50 outlets under development in existing airports?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a blend of already-announced airports such as Delhi, Navi Mumbai and Bhogapuram; these were won 3-8 months ago and are in build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Highways strategy: is it accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said highways are a medium-to-long-term opportunity tied to government wayside amenity plans, with a return threshold that must be met; it will be calibrated, not immediate.

risks_watch: International traffic recovery depends on airline route restorations from September-October 2026; Middle East conflict renewed in June.
EBITDA margin (35.8%) under pressure from pre-operating and employee costs at new airports; watch normalisation in next 12 months.
Delhi T3 contract ends 30 September 2026 and the GHL JV bid outcome is unknown; it moves out of consolidation.
Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28 may bring cost resets.
PAT growth flattered by INR131 million one-time GST write-back; underlying growth is lower.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and balance sheet, but cautious on near-term traffic; management repeatedly attributes weakness to temporary external factors. Evasive on specific numbers such as net contract gain targets and JV economics, and on the Delhi T3 bid outcome.
key_quotes: Despite the disruptions arising from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, we delivered double -digit growth in both sales and profitability, continued to expand our network, and further strengthened our position across key airport markets.
So, in a sense, if you see, we tend to be in that range of more than passenger traffic, somewhere in the 5% to 7% above that at least in terms of performance.
Those are the leverages that we tend to enjoy, in terms of bringing the required economies of scale.
In the new SPV, our shareholding with GMR is 30% and therefore it doesn't get consolidated going forward.

So, the investment is already made, the capacity is in place, and we are ready. When traffic returns, and history tells us it will, TFS is well -positioned to benefit from the network and groundwork we have put in place over the past 12 months.

growth.why: Q1 consolidated revenue rose 20.6% YoY to INR4.5bn with 580 outlets, net contract gains of 15.9% and over 50 outlets under development mostly opening in FY27; offset by flat passenger traffic, 0.8% system LFL and a renewal rate dip from ~94% to 92%, with H2 traffic recovery expected but unquantified.
